head: 63bc3e57
headSubject: feat(SEC-3): real ProcessBuilder child process for plugin IPC (Model B step 2)
summary: Committed and pushed SEC-3 Model B step 1 (was left uncommitted last session). Implemented and shipped step 2 per docs/architecture/PLUGIN_PROCESS_ISOLATION_DESIGN.md section 6: PluginIpcChildProcessMain (real child-process entry point) + PluginIpcChildProcess (host-side ProcessBuilder spawner with crash detection, remapping a closed channel to PLUGIN_EXECUTION_PROCESS_KILLED once the process is confirmed dead). Found and fixed two real bugs along the way: (1) a raw -cp <classpath> argument hits Windows CreateProcess error=206 (filename or extension too long) against the assembled sample app's real multi-jar classpath -- fixed with a java @argfile; (2) an off-by-one in the new PluginIpcChildProcessTest's System.exit-scenario assertion. Live-fires SEC-3's own two named done-when tests over a real OS process boundary (System.exit doesn't take down host; forbidden callback denied). Full run-runtimehost-gate.ps1 verified green after two red iterations, each root-caused via a narrow --tests rerun rather than re-running the full ~8min gate blind. ledger/items/SEC-3.yml updated with full step-2 detail, status left OPEN (memory/CPU still unbounded until step 4). Two commits pushed to main: 126e012e (step 1) and 63bc3e57 (step 2).
nextStep: SEC-3 step 3 per docs/architecture/PLUGIN_PROCESS_ISOLATION_DESIGN.md section 6: the fixed-size warm pool of fungible worker processes (design section 2) -- pool sizing (npdev.runtime.plugin-pool-size config), idle recycling (N invocations + wall-clock idle timer), host shutdown handling (@PreDestroy close-frame then destroyForcibly), and real plugin-JAR classloading via RuntimePluginPackageRealizationService (a fungible worker needs the plugin JAR path + class name to travel in the invoke frame itself, since step 2's one-process-per-invoke model got away with binding the handler class at process-spawn time via a command-line arg -- that shortcut goes away once workers are pooled and reused across different plugins). This is materially bigger than steps 1-2 (new pooling infrastructure, not just a stream-source swap) -- worth scoping/confirming approach before implementing. After that, step 4 (Linux cgroups v2 / Windows Job Objects) is what actually closes the item's memory/CPU done-when bar.
verified: Local: full run-runtimehost-gate.ps1 green (assembled sample app's own gradle test task BUILD SUCCESSFUL across 665 tests incl. the 3 new PluginIpcChildProcessTest cases, runtimehost-core's own gradle test task BUILD SUCCESSFUL, coverage-floor + runtime-surface-evidence checks all passed). headSubject: fix(QUAL-53): clone-port file lock, Windows PermissionError treated as real failure
summary: Investigated and fixed the one lead from the last handoff: NPDevCli/tests/test_monitor_clone.py::test_concurrent_calls_never_collide's Windows PermissionError. Confirmed it reproduces reliably when run as part of the full test file (not in isolation), stress-tested the underlying create-vs-unlink race standalone (12 threads, 300 iterations each: 2719 FileExistsError vs 15 PermissionError, ~1 in 180), and traced it to _acquire_file_lock in NPDevCli/npdev_monitor.py only catching FileExistsError. Fixed by also catching PermissionError in the retry loop (QUAL-53, commit a0e245b1, pushed).
